topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and sets the learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Biological Foundations of Cancer and Drivers of Mutation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary, microenvironment-dependent genetic disease and outline the balance of intrinsic, inherited, and environmental factors driving DNA damage.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk and analyze epidemiological data and public debates comparing environmental causes with random biological chance.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the role of viruses, bacteria, and parasites in oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma to illustrate how infection and immune perturbation drive malignant transformation.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mechanisms of DNA Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which radiation and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts, mutations, and oxidative damage.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion and Non-Mutagenic Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish cancer initiators from promoters by showing how non-mutagenic stimuli such as asbestos and phorbol esters drive chronic inflammation and cell proliferation.

topics.label: Host Susceptibility, Developmental Timing, and Mechanistic Synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze how host developmental windows and tissue specificity influence carcinogenic risk and synthesize the core mechanistic principles of cancer development.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine whether agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Carcinogen Risk-Benefit Appraisal and Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by evaluating the practical trade-offs between carcinogen exposure risks and daily life benefits.
